name: LT1122 (grades A/B/C/D)
tagline: Linear Tech's 14 MHz, 80 V/µs, 340 ns-settling JFET single; a niche roller's pick for DAC output and filter stages.

lineage.note: Sole source. Poly-gate JFET process, aimed at 12-bit data conversion. Macromodel header dated 1990; intro date unconfirmed.
Bought LTC in 2017. Hosts the LTC datasheet 1122fb (Rev B, 02/14) unchanged; no die change found.

part_numbers.note: Base part; single only. Listed on ADI product page; lifecycle not shown.
A grade, PDIP-8; #PBF is RoHS. diyAudio reportedly calls it 'a good chip'.
B grade, PDIP-8. Seen in an EasyEDA/LCSC library (2020-07-06).
C grade, PDIP-8. Listed at Mouser c. 2019–2020.
D grade, PDIP-8. Seen in an EasyEDA/LCSC library (2020-07-06).
SO-8; exact order codes unconfirmed. DS8 possibly marked 'OBSOLETE PACKAGE'.

key_specs.value: 7 mA (Mouser: 7.5 mA typ; 7.8 mA also seen)
P-channel JFET pair, 2.25 mA tail current

reputation.summary: A niche pick. Head-Fi rollers list it with the LT1361, LT1364 and LT1469 for DAC output stages. diyAudio members group it with the LT1028 and LT1115 as LTC chips worth trying. Tangent's notes (Soomal, 2005) list it to test later. No ASR or Samuel Groner measurements. A KiCad HP 3458A A3 reproduction uses it as buffer U404.
typical_uses: Single op-amp rolling in DIP-8 sockets
Precision instrument buffers, e.g. HP 3458A A3 U404
caveats: Single channel only: dual sockets need an adapter carrying two.
About 7 mA quiescent per amplifier; runs warmer and drains batteries faster than TL07x parts.
Fast part (14 MHz, 80 V/µs): decouple well and keep leads short.
Grades A–D probably differ in DC or settling guarantees; unlikely to matter for audio.
Marketed for speed, not low noise; voltage noise and THD are unconfirmed.

counterfeit_notes: No LT1122 fakes reported. Buy from authorized distributors; distrust cheap 'LT1122ACN8' lots. Check logo, grade letter and date code, and confirm about 7 mA at ±15 V. A remarked TL071 would draw far less current and be much slower.
